name: Broad-nib pen
summary: A pen with a flat, square-cut tip held at a fixed angle, so the width of a stroke changes with its direction and the stress of the letter is diagonal.
how: Hold the nib edge at 30–45° to the baseline and keep that angle for every stroke.
Make the stem width 4–5 nib widths of the x-height in a book hand and 3–4 in a broken hand.
Let the thin parts fall on the diagonal of the nib angle, so the o has its thinnest points at about 11 and 5 o'clock.

origin.note: The pen is older than print; Gutenberg cut his textura from the broad-nib book hand of the scribes, the first record of the pen in type.

adoptions.via: Gutenberg's textura for the 42-line Bible copies the broken broad-nib hand.
Nicolas Jenson cuts a roman with the diagonal stress of the humanist broad-nib hand.
Edward Johnston, a calligrapher, draws the London Underground sans from broad-nib proportions.
